standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the local normal form S = Spec(A), U = Spec(A[x, 1/g]/(f)) with f monic and f' invertible; the identification of that algebra as a localisation of a finite locally free A-algebra is the counted step.

core_obligations: Localise the question: replace S and U by affine neighbourhoods of s and of u, so that h may be assumed to be a standard etale morphism of affines, and write S = Spec(A), U = Spec(A[x, 1/g]/(f)) with f monic and f' invertible in A[x, 1/g] (proof lines 365-370).

Exhibit U as an open subscheme of a finite locally free S-scheme: use A[x, 1/g]/(f) = (A[x]/(f))_g, so that U embeds as a localisation of the finite free A-algebra A[x]/(f) and therefore into T = Spec(A[x]/(f)), which is finite locally free over S (proof lines 371-374).

Conclude by reducing the equivalence to the already-proved finite locally free case lemma-finite-flat-weak-assassin-up-down applied to the flat morphism T -> S and the chosen points of T (proof lines 374-376).
proof_roadmap: Work locally on source and target; etale morphisms are locally standard etale, so assume S and U affine and h given by a monic f with invertible derivative (proof lines 365-370).
Identify A[x, 1/g]/(f) with the localisation (A[x]/(f))_g, hence U with an open subscheme of T = Spec(A[x]/(f)), which is finite locally free over S (proof lines 371-373).
Apply the finite locally free version of the weak-association statement to T -> S, which is flat, to get the asserted equivalence at the points u and s (proof lines 374-376).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that for an etale h : U -> S the weakly associated points of h^*G over u are exactly the weakly associated points of G over the image s (statement lines 354-361). The step that is not a routine citation is the observation that a standard etale A-algebra A[x, 1/g]/(f) is a localisation of the finite free A-algebra A[x]/(f), so that U can be viewed as an open subscheme of a scheme T which is finite locally free, hence flat, over S; only then does the previously proved finite-flat version of the statement apply (proof lines 371-376). Everything else is localisation of the problem to affine neighbourhoods, so the claim is H2.
